meta.project: Bilingual, Ontology-Aware, and Explainable ESG Intelligence System
meta.description: Comprehensive mapping of integrated research objectives to curated literature corpus, establishing causal traceability from expected contributions to empirical evidence.

research_questions: RQ1.1: How can Transformer-based architectures be optimized for bilingual ESG ABSA?
RQ1.3: How can regional calibration and ESG lexicons mitigate bias?

literature_references.title: Morphosyntactic Tagging with Pre-trained Language Models for Arabic and its Dialects
literature_references.authors: Go Inoue, Salam Khalifa, Nizar Habash
literature_references.relevance: Provides empirical justification for C1 and RQ1.3 by demonstrating that pre-trained language models can be successfully adapted to low-resource dialects and regional variations through strategic fine-tuning.

literature_references.title: Towards Offensive Language Identification for Dravidian Languages
literature_references.relevance: Supports C3 and RQ1.1 by exploring zero-shot and few-shot cross-lingual transfer learning in multilingual transformer networks (XLM-R, mBERT) for low-resource language settings.

contributions: C8: Large-scale ESG LLM benchmark (30+ models)
research_questions: RQ2.1: To what extent does few-shot learning improve ESG granularity?
RQ2.4: How can multi-LLM fusion reduce hallucination?
RQ2.2: How can long-context mechanisms enhance scalability?

literature_references.title: Cutting Down on Prompts and Parameters: Simple Few-Shot Learning with Language Models
literature_references.authors: Robert L. Logan, Ivana Balazevic, Eric Wallace, Fabio Petroni, Sameer Singh, Sebastian Riedel
literature_references.relevance: Directly addresses RQ2.1 and C16 by validating that few-shot learning with minimal parameter updates can achieve high accuracy in specialized domains with sparse labeled data.

literature_references.title: PandaLM: An Automatic Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Instruction Tuning Optimization
literature_references.relevance: Provides a methodology for C8 by introducing automated benchmarking frameworks to evaluate LLMs as judges, essential for the systematic performance baselines of Objective 2.

research_questions: RQ3.1: How can symbolic reasoning be integrated using ESG ontologies?
RQ3.2: How can transparent outputs be ensured via reasoning graphs?

literature_references.title: Representing Rule-based Chatbots with Transformers
literature_references.authors: Dan Friedman, Abhishek Panigrahi, Danqi Chen
literature_references.relevance: Establishes the technical foundation for C7 and RQ3.1 by demonstrating how transformer architectures can implement interpretable symbolic mechanisms and long-term state tracking.

literature_references.title: XPrompt: Explaining Large Language Model's Generation via Joint Prompt Attribution
literature_references.authors: Yurui Chang, Bochuan Cao, Yujia Wang, Jinghui Chen, Lu Lin
literature_references.relevance: Supports C15 and RQ3.2 by providing a counterfactual framework for joint prompt attribution, enabling the explainable neuro-symbolic reasoning required for this layer.

research_questions: RQ4.1: How can XAI improve stakeholder trust in ESG outputs?
RQ4.5: Can tone–outcome mismatch reliably indicate greenwashing?

literature_references.title: A Probabilistic Framework for LLM Hallucination Detection via Belief Tree Propagation
literature_references.authors: Bairu Hou, Yang Zhang, Jacob Andreas, Shiyu Chang
literature_references.relevance: Justifies C11 and RQ4.5 by introducing structured belief trees to detect inconsistencies in LLM-generated statements, a prerequisite for quantifying greenwashing risk.

literature_references.title: Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models
literature_references.relevance: Addresses RQ4.1 and the trust gap by providing systematic study on model failures (hallucinations), which is critical for establishing risk intelligence layers.

research_questions: RQ5.1: How can transparent and auditable outputs be ensured?
RQ5.2: How can reasoning quality and consistency be operationalized at scale?

literature_references.title: Seq1F1B: Efficient Sequence-Level Pipeline Parallelism for Large Language Model Training
literature_references.relevance: Supports the scalability requirements of RQ5.2 and C12 by introducing efficient scheduling for long sequences, enabling the system to process massive institutional disclosures.

literature_references.title: Babysit A Language Model From Scratch: Interactive Language Learning by Trials and Demonstrations
literature_references.authors: Ziqiao Ma, Zekun Wang, Joyce Chai
literature_references.relevance: Validates the iterative dashboard and human-in-the-loop design in C12, showing how interactive corrective feedback loops improve learning efficiency and decision readiness.
